CanonicalVars.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 24.) All 23 cards now store their printed C# var under a `_`-attribute (or, for 3 cards whose C# var is a live/computed value at display time -- guilty, normality, expect_a_fight -- a `magic_number` property override; wither similarly overrides `base_damage`) so `Card.base_damage`/`base_block`/`base_hp_loss`/`magic_number` report the C# value instead of the 0/None default. Two additive base.py changes: `_frail` added to `_MAGIC_ATTRS` (shame) and a new `base_gold` property (debt, spoils_map -- GoldVar had no base property at all). feel_no_pain's `_block` was renamed to `_power_amount` (fixing a WRONG value, not just a missing one -- `base_block` no longer misreports it as block-granting; matches Rage/Corruption/Stampede's DynamicVar('Power', ...) convention). Combat behavior / dealt numbers are byte-identical in every case -- a printed-number / observation-encoder fix only. 3 of the 23 (debt, spoils_map, rolling_boulder's secondary IncrementAmount) have NO obs-vector change despite the API fix (full_env.py has no base_gold read site; magic_number carries one number per card and _power_amount dominates rolling_boulder's scan) -- documented, not closed further. CHECKPOINT NOTE for training: encoded VALUES changed for the other 20 cards in feature slots f[17]/f[18] damage, f[20]/f[21] block, f[22] hp_loss, f[23] magic_number; obs LAYOUT unchanged. The text it replaced read: `new DamageVar(9m, ValueProp.Move)` maps to `_damage = 9`, but `new HpLossVar(1m)` (Breakthrough.cs:13-17) has no `_hp_loss` in `_init_vars`, so `Card.base_hp_loss` reports 0. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed DynamicVar with no corresponding `_`-attribute in `_init_vars`, so the sim's printed-number API reports the default and `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card wrongly for the policy. OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The self-damage goes through the damage pipeline. Breakthrough.cs:27 is `CreatureCmd.Damage(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.HpLoss.BaseValue, Unblockable | Unpowered | Move, this)` and cards/breakthrough.py now calls `DamageCmd.deal(..., props=UNBLOCKABLE|UNPOWERED|MOVE, dealer=player, card=self)` in its place. WAS: a hand-rolled `p.hp = max(0, p.hp - 1)` with a bare on_hp_changed and a manual should_die/on_death, so `on_damage_received` never fired, no damage modifier was consulted, and the Intangible cap and Buffer were skipped. EXECUTED: play Breakthrough holding Rupture 1 and the player now gains 1 Strength (RupturePower.cs:44-57, the null-cardSource immediate-apply branch) where the sim gained none. The two props are pinned separately -- 20 block does not absorb the 1 HP (Unblockable) and Strength 5 does not scale it while it DOES scale the 9-damage AoE half (Unpowered). `HP_LOSS = 1` is HpLossVar(1m), Breakthrough.cs:16, with no upgrade and no ascension branch. Pinned by test/test_card_residue_gaps2.py (4 tests). NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: The AoE half is faithful (`DamageCmd.Attack(9).FromCard(this).TargetingAllOpponents(CombatState)`, Breakthrough.cs:28-30, == a per-enemy `DamageCmd.deal(..., dealer=ctx.player, card=self)`), and so is the order (self-damage FIRST). THE SELF-DAMAGE BYPASSES THE DAMAGE PIPELINE ENTIRELY. C# calls `CreatureCmd.Damage(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.HpLoss.BaseValue, Unblockable | Unpowered | Move, this)` (Breakthrough.cs:27) -- the full pipeline: the damage modifiers, the damage cap, `Hook.AfterCurrentHpChanged`, `Hook.AfterDamageReceived`, the death check and Kill. The sim hand-rolls it: `p.hp = max(0, p.hp - 1)` plus a bare `on_hp_changed` and a manual `should_die`/`on_death` (breakthrough.py:42-50), so `on_damage_received` never fires and no damage modifier is consulted. Observable through RupturePower, which gains Strength on any unblocked damage its owner receives (`RupturePower.AfterDamageReceived`, RupturePower.cs:44-57 -- with cardSource null the immediate-apply branch at line 48 is taken) and whose sim port listens on `on_damage_received` (powers.py:272-289). Play Breakthrough holding Rupture: the game gains Strength, the sim does not. LIVE -- card/rupture is a ported Ironclad card (sts2_rl/cards/rupture_card.py) and Breakthrough is a ported Common. The bypass also skips the Intangible cap and Buffer, which would matter for any larger card-sourced HP loss. Presentation, folded in: VfxCmd.PlayOnCreatureCenter (26) and WithHitFx (29).

guards.what: the enemy loop skips on `enemy.is_dead`, not `enemy.is_gone` (breakthrough.py:54)
guards.issue: Every other AoE card in the sim filters on `not e.is_gone` (conflagration, shockwave, omnislice, sword_boomerang, rip_and_tear -- see `py audit/tools/card_probes.py dead-target-guards`), and `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46). Breakthrough alone uses `is_dead`, so an ESCAPED-but-alive enemy is still struck. C#'s `TargetingAllOpponents(CombatState)` resolves against the combat's live opponent list, from which an escaped creature has been removed (`CreatureCmd.Escape`, CreatureCmd.cs:579-603). DORMANT: no ported Ironclad-reachable monster escapes while a second enemy is still alive to keep the combat running, so the extra target is never reached today; live with any ported escaping monster in a multi-enemy fight.

Verified by DIFFERENTIAL EXECUTION against a reconstructed pre-edit subclass over 48 configurations (hp x seed x encounter size x first-enemy-dead): zero differences in HP, piles, powers, energy, phase, result, or the full ordered HookSystem dispatch trace. If that bail moves, weakens, or is reordered behind a hook, Breakthrough regresses SILENTLY and the tests in this record will NOT catch it -- they assert outcomes downstream of the bail.
